subject: biology

concepts.title: Cellular Respiration and Substrates
concepts.definition: The biochemical process occurring within cells where chemical bonds of organic compounds are indeed oxidised to liberate energy stored as ATP.
concepts.key_idea: Energy stored in organic nutrients is harvested through controlled enzymatic oxidation to synthesise ATP.
question_patterns: what is cellular respiration and what are respiratory substrates
define respiratory substrates with examples
explain how plants manage gas exchange without dedicated respiratory organs
why is respiration considered an enzymatic stepwise oxidation process

solution_steps.explain: Carbohydrates, fats, or proteins act as substrates for intracellular enzymatic oxidation.
Oxidation converts bond energy step-by-step into high-energy phosphate bonds of ATP.

concepts.title: Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)
concepts.definition: A ten-step anaerobic cytoplasmic pathway where one molecule of glucose is partially oxidised into two molecules of pyruvic acid.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Glucose splits into two pyruvic acid molecules in the cytoplasm without consuming molecular oxygen.
question_patterns: calculate net ATP formed directly during glycolysis
find the direct ATP yield in glycolytic breakdown
determine the net gain of ATP in cytoplasm from glucose conversion to pyruvate
what is the net direct ATP output of glycolysis given total formed and consumed

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the ATP consumed in initial steps from the total ATP produced in substrate-level phosphorylation.

concepts.title: Fermentation
concepts.definition: An anaerobic metabolic breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid or ethanol and carbon dioxide with low energy release.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Incomplete oxidation under anaerobic conditions yields metabolic byproducts and regenerates NAD+.
question_patterns: explain alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation
what are the key enzymes involved in fermentation
compare energy release in anaerobic fermentation versus aerobic oxidation
why do yeast cells die when alcohol level reaches around 13 percent

solution_steps.explain: Decarboxylation and reduction turn pyruvate into ethanol or lactate.
Less than 7% of total chemical energy in glucose is liberated during fermentation.

concepts.title: Link Reaction and Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) Cycle
concepts.definition: A mitochondrial matrix pathway where acetyl-CoA condenses with oxaloacetate to undergo cyclic decarboxylation and oxidation.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Pyruvate undergoes oxidative decarboxylation to form acetyl-CoA, which fuels the cyclic generation of reduced coenzymes.
question_patterns: describe the steps of Krebs cycle starting from acetyl CoA
what is the link reaction connecting glycolysis to the TCA cycle
list the primary products synthesized per turn of the citric acid cycle
where does the tricarboxylic acid cycle take place within the cell

solution_steps.explain: Pyruvate dehydrogenase converts pyruvate to acetyl-CoA in the mitochondrial matrix.
Acetyl-CoA condenses with oxaloacetic acid to yield citrate, generating CO2, NADH, FADH2, and GTP.

concepts.title: Electron Transport System and Oxidative Phosphorylation
concepts.definition: A chain of inner mitochondrial membrane protein complexes that transfer electrons to oxygen while creating a proton gradient for ATP synthesis.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Flow of electrons through respiratory complexes drives proton pumping across the inner membrane to power ATP synthase.
question_patterns: explain the electron transport system in mitochondria
how does oxidative phosphorylation synthesize ATP via proton gradient
what is the role of oxygen in the electron transport chain
describe the structural components and function of ATP synthase complex V

solution_steps.explain: Electrons from NADH and FADH2 pass through complexes I-IV to terminal oxygen.
Protons pass back into matrix through F0 channel driving F1 to synthesize ATP from ADP and Pi.

concepts.title: Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation
concepts.definition: A quantitative accounting of total theoretical ATP produced from complete oxidation of one glucose molecule.
concepts.key_idea: Total theoretical yield is determined by summing direct ATP both synthesis and ATP generated from coenzyme oxidation.
question_patterns: calculate total ATP generated given counts of NADH FADH2 and direct ATP
compute the net theoretical ATP yield from full oxidation of glucose
find overall ATP synthesis from given reduced coenzymes and substrate level phosphorylation
how much total ATP is obtained when given quantities of NADH and FADH2 pass through ETS

solution_steps.explain: Each NADH yields 3 ATP molecules via oxidative phosphorylation.
Each FADH2 yields 2 ATP molecules via oxidative phosphorylation.
Add ATP from NADH, FADH2, and direct substrate-level phosphorylation.

concepts.title: Amphibolic Pathway
concepts.definition: A metabolic pathway that functions in both catabolic breaking-down operations and anabolic biosynthetic construction.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Respiratory intermediates act as precursor molecules for anabolic synthesis of lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates.
question_patterns: why is the respiratory pathway referred to as an amphibolic pathway
explain how respiratory intermediates are involved in anabolic reactions
discuss the dual catabolic and anabolic roles of acetyl CoA and TCA cycle intermediates
justify calling respiration amphibolic rather than purely catabolic

solution_steps.explain: Carbohydrates, fats, and proteins break down into respiratory intermediates to generate energy.
Intermediates like acetyl-CoA or oxaloacetate are withdrawn from the pathway to synthesize fatty acids or amino acids.

concepts.title: Respiratory Quotient (RQ)
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the volume's numerical ratio of carbon dioxide given out to the volume of oxygen absorbed during biological respiration.
concepts.key_idea: The ratio of CO2 produced to O2 consumed depends directly on the chemical nature of the respired substrate.
question_patterns: calculate the respiratory quotient given evolved carbon dioxide and consumed oxygen
find the RQ value when given volumes of CO2 evolved and O2 consumed
compute the respiratory ratio for a given substrate combustion
what is the value of respiratory quotient when volume of CO2 is divided by volume of O2

solution_steps.action: calculate ratio of CO2 to O2
solution_steps.explain: Divide the volume or molar quantity of carbon dioxide evolved by oxygen consumed.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the Respiratory Quotient (RQ) for the oxidation of tripalmitin when {volume_co2} moles of CO2 are released and {volume_o2} moles of O2 are consumed.

solution_template.action: calculate ratio of CO2 to O2
solution_template.explain: Divide the volume or moles of carbon dioxide released by oxygen consumed.

solution_template.explain: Each NADH yields 3 ATP molecules via oxidative phosphorylation.
Each FADH2 yields 2 ATP molecules via oxidative phosphorylation.
Add ATP from NADH, FADH2, and direct substrate-level phosphorylation.

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a glycolytic pathway, if {formed_atp} ATP molecules are formed directly through substrate level phosphorylation and {used_atp} ATP molecules are consumed during initial phosphorylation steps, find the net direct ATP gained.

solution_template.explain: Subtract the ATP consumed in initial steps from the total ATP produced in substrate-level phosphorylation.
